title: Parametric Systems
objective: Panelise a facade and cut an adjustable opening into every panel.
learn: Chaining several operations into one adjustable system.

nodes.need: a component that fills the closed outline with a flat surface
nodes.hint: Surface › Freeform. The outline is closed and planar.
nodes.correct: Boundary Surfaces fills closed planar curves with a trimmed flat surface — our facade becomes something we can subdivide.

wrong.loft: Loft needs two or more section curves to skin between.
wrong.extrude: Extrude would push the outline into a box, not fill it.
wrong.pipe: Pipe makes a tube around the outline.
wrong.offset: Offset makes a parallel copy of the outline — still just a curve.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that fills the closed outline with a flat surface.

nodes.need: a way to split the surface’s UV space into a grid of cells
nodes.hint: Maths › Domain. Surfaces live in a 2D (U×V) domain.
nodes.correct: Divide Domain² splits the surface’s 2D domain into U columns × V rows of sub-domains. It doesn’t make geometry yet — it’s a cutting plan.

wrong.range: Range divides a 1D domain into numbers. A surface needs a 2D grid.
wrong.series: Series makes a list of numbers, not UV cells.
wrong.divideCurve: Divide Curve works on curves, not surfaces.
wrong.graft: Graft restructures data; it can’t subdivide anything.
wrong.*: This slot needs a way to split the surface’s UV space into a grid of cells.

nodes.need: a component that cuts the surface into pieces using the UV grid
nodes.correct: Isotrim (SubSrf) cuts one sub-surface per UV cell — your facade panels.

wrong.listItem: List Item would pick one cell description, not cut the surface.
wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces is already in place upstream.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that cuts the surface into pieces using the UV grid.

nodes.need: a component that finds the centre of each panel
nodes.hint: Surface › Analysis. It returns area and centroid.
nodes.correct: Area returns each panel’s area and, more usefully here, its Centroid — the point we’ll scale around.

wrong.constructPoint: Construct Point needs coordinates we don’t have. Area computes centres for us.
wrong.listItem: List Item picks items; it doesn’t measure anything.
wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter just stores points.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that finds the centre of each panel.

nodes.need: a transform that shrinks each panel around its centre
nodes.correct: Scale shrinks each panel around its own centroid by the Opening factor. One slider now controls every opening on the facade.

wrong.move: Move shifts panels; it can’t make openings.
wrong.rotate: Rotate would spin panels out of the facade plane.
wrong.offset: Offset works on curves and can fail on corners; Scale is cleaner here.
wrong.mirror: Mirror flips panels; nothing gets smaller.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that shrinks each panel around its centre.

check.prompt: Which input of Isotrim receives the Divide Domain² grid?
check.hint: S = the surface to cut, D = the domains to cut by.
check.correct: D takes the sub-domains. One surface × many domains = many panels.

wrong.S: S is the base surface — Boundary Surfaces is already plugged in.
